title: Factors Influencing Speciation Changes of Hexavalent Chromium and Distribution Correlations between Chromium and Other Elements in Chromium Slag Field Soil in North China
content: This study investigated the main factors involved in the speciation transformation of Cr(VI) and linkages between elements of soil from chromium slag field using chro-mium contaminated soil from North China. The study utilized macro condition ex-periments and in-situ micro-XRF fluorescence spectroscopy (μ-XRF) to com-prehen-sively elucidate the transformation mechanisms and elemental interrelationships. The findings indicated that under acidic conditions (pH< 7), there is a notable increase in reduction efficiency due to the conversion of Cr (VI) from CrO₄²⁻ to HCrO₄⁻/Cr₂O₇²⁻. The hierarchy of reducing agent efficiency follows the order of FeSO₄  > citric acid  > fulvic acid. Temperature variations (-20℃ to 30℃) had minimal impact on Cr (VI) transformation, while reducing humidity indirectly reduced Cr(VI) levels by promoting the diffusion of the reducing agent and microbial metabolism, albeit to a lesser extent compared to chemical interventions. Variations in soil mechanical composition led to uneven distribution of Cr (VI). Larger particles (>0.2 mm) in BC-35 and BC-36-4 served as the main reservoirs of Cr (VI) by accumulating Fe and Mn oxides. In contrast, the Cr (VI) content in smaller particles (< 0.074 mm) of BC-36-3 increased as particle size decreased, contrary to the typical expectation of higher Cr (VI) content in finer particles. Micro-X-ray fluorescence (μ-XRF) and Pearson correlation analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between chromium (Cr) and calcium (Ca), iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), and nickel (Ni) (Pearson coefficient  >0.7, p < 0.01). Conversely, chromium showed a weak correlation with magnesium (Mg), aluminum (Al), silicon (Si), and potassium (K). This suggests a dual mechanism involving oxidation-reduction coupling through coordinated adsorption and electron transfer on the surface of iron and manganese oxides. Through a combined "macro-micro" analytical approach, the study elucidated the complex factors in-fluencing the presence of hexavalent chromium (Cr (VI)) in soil at chromium slag dis-posal sites. These findings provide valuable insights to guide remediation strategies for chromium-contaminated soil.
